problem: IBM said it wanted better collaboration and a faster pace of work.
title: IBM tells many remote workers to relocate to an office or leave
context: IBM had been a pioneer of remote work, and remote staff were reported at up to 40 percent of its workforce.
decision_made: Require remote staff in affected units to move to a regional office within 30 days or leave.
action_taken: Started in marketing and software and systems units in 2016 to 2017, with the policy expected to spread.
observed_outcome: Reaction was critical and other firms were also recalling remote workers. A 2024 report showed IBM again requiring U.S. managers to return to the office or leave.
lessons: Even long-standing remote programmes can be reversed when leaders prioritise in-person collaboration.
limitations: No data on productivity or retention was found. The initial scope was reported by media and not detailed by IBM.

claims.claim_text: IBM gave remote workers a choice between relocating to a regional office and leaving the company.
IBM said the change would improve collaboration and accelerate the pace of work.
